describe: print messages to the serial monitor
guide: Start the serial port once in setup() with Serial.begin(9600); then Serial.println("..."); wherever something happens in loop().
report: The sketch prints "LED on" and "LED off" to the serial monitor now$extra. Open Nest can't show the serial monitor yet; in the Arduino IDE it is Tools > Serial Monitor, at 9600 baud.
It talks to the computer now: "LED on" and "LED off"$extra, at 9600 baud. You can read it in the Arduino IDE's Serial Monitor -- Open Nest doesn't have one yet.
teach: Serial.begin(9600) opens the USB connection at 9600 bits a second, and Serial.println sends one line of text down it.
